pageTitle: CrossShelf — All your games. One library.
description: Your Steam, GOG and Epic libraries in one Windows app. Browse your collection, search for games and see where you own them. Free and open source.
heroBody: Bring your Steam, GOG and Epic libraries together. Browse your whole collection, find any game and see where you own it.
heroAlt: CrossShelf demo library with Celeste and other real games, store tabs and a game detail panel.
example: Real games · simulated library and accounts
exampleBanner: DEMO DATA · REAL GAMES · SIMULATED LIBRARY
artworkDisclaimer: Demo library: accounts, ownership and wishlists are simulated. Game artwork and trademarks belong to their respective owners. CrossShelf is not affiliated with or endorsed by the stores, developers or publishers shown.
previewBody: A game gets one row, even when you own it in more than one store. The store tabs tell you where it is yours, shared by family, or still on a wishlist.
libraryAlt: CrossShelf demo library: real games grouped across Steam, GOG and Epic, with simulated ownership and Steam family access shown separately.
reviewAlt: Example wishlist review: Hades on a simulated Steam wishlist compared with an Epic copy, with evidence and manual review controls.
connectionsAlt: Example connections screen with fictional accounts, library counts and the capabilities of each store.
libraryCaption: Search once. See every store, your own copies and Steam family access.
reviewCaption: Compare the wish with your copy. Check the edition and choose what to keep.
connectionsCaption: Connect on each store’s official sign-in page, then sync from the app.
playsAlt: Example Play log board: real games in Playing, Backlog, Paused, Completed and Dropped columns, with simulated hours and a tray of suggestions above.
playsCaption: Board, list or diary. Drag each game to its column; hours come from Steam.
cleanupBody: A similar title is a reason to look closer. Check the game, edition and platform side by side, then mark only the wishes you want to remove.
cleanupPoint: Nothing leaves a wishlist until you review and confirm the batch.
cleanupAlt: CrossShelf demo review showing real games with simulated wishlist entries, owned copies and the option to keep a wish.
playBody: Note what you are playing, what is waiting and what you have finished, whichever store it is in. The diary orders your games by the last time you played and adds up the week’s hours.
playPoint: Suggestions come from your play time, and nothing moves until you click.
diaryAlt: Example diary: real games grouped by last session, with simulated hours, this week’s hours and states to confirm.
howBody: No API keys or terminal. Install the app and use the accounts you already have.
stepConnectBody: Sign in on the official Steam, GOG and Epic pages. CrossShelf never asks for your password.
stepSyncBody: Sync, search and filter your games. Steam family access is always labelled separately.
stepReviewBody: Choose the Steam and GOG wishes to remove, review the batch and confirm. The app checks each result.
localTitle: Your shelf lives on your PC.
localBody: No CrossShelf account. No telemetry. Your library stays on your computer, and saved sessions are encrypted with Windows data protection.
localDetail: Export your library and wishlists to CSV or JSON, and your plays and decisions to a file you can import on another computer.
faqStoresBody: Read your Steam, GOG and Epic libraries, plus Steam family access. Read and clean Steam and GOG wishlists. For Epic wishlists, the app opens the store website; reading and removal are not available in the app. Hours played come from Steam; GOG and Epic hours will follow once they are checked with real accounts.
faqFamily: Does family access count as owning a game?
faqFamilyBody: Family access is labelled separately and excluded from cleanup by default. You can include it in Settings, where it remains a separate reason to review a wish.
faqWindows: What do I need to run it?
faqWindowsBody: Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11, 64-bit. The installer runs for your user without administrator permissions and downloads WebView2 if it is missing.
faqWarning: Why might Windows show a warning?
faqWarningBody: The installer is not signed with a publisher certificate, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run. If you downloaded it from this project’s GitHub release, choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
faqPriceBody: Yes. CrossShelf is free and open source under the MIT licence. It does not install or launch games, buy anything, or transfer game licences.
noScript: This is the English version. Enable JavaScript to switch languages, choose screenshots and resolve the direct installer link.
